BASELINE = {pb.name: (pb.rotation_mode, pb.rotation_euler.copy(),
                      pb.rotation_quaternion.copy(), pb.location.copy())
            for pb in ctrl.pose.bones}

reset()
REST = snap()
RIGID = rigid(REST)

print("\n" + "=" * 72)
print("WHICH CONTROLS ACTUALLY DO ANYTHING")
print("(35 deg rotation / 0.5 location; 'TEARS' = a joint length changed >5%)")
print(f"\n{'bone':28s}{'mode':5s} | parts moved | rigid?")
skip = ("MCH_", "ORG_", "VIS_", "DEF_")
rows = []
for pb in list(ctrl.pose.bones):

    for mode in ("rot", "loc"):

        b = ctrl.pose.bones[pb.name]

        else:
            b.location = Vector((0, 0, 0.5))
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        st = snap()
        moved = [p for p in parts
                 if (st[p][1] - REST[p][1]).length > 0.02 or (st[p][0] - REST[p][0]).length > 0.02]
        if not moved:
            continue
        now = rigid(st)
        worst = max(abs(now[k] - RIGID[k]) for k in RIGID) if RIGID else 0.0
        tag = "ok" if worst < 0.05 * max(RIGID.values()) else f"TEARS ({worst:.3f})"
        rows.append((pb.name, mode, moved, tag))
        print(f"{pb.name:28s}{mode:5s} | {len(moved):2d} {', '.join(moved[:4])}{'...' if len(moved) > 4 else ''} | {tag}")

print("\n" + "=" * 72)
print("USABLE CONTROLS (move something, keep joints rigid):")
for name, mode, moved, tag in rows:
    if tag == "ok":
        print(f"   {name:28s} {mode}  -> {', '.join(moved[:5])}")
print("\nNEXT: sweep each usable control per axis to learn its convention")
print("(which axis is forward/twist/lean), then author a spec for anim_render.py.")

"""FK probe + offline joint-angle solver for the community R15 rig.

    blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python fk_probe.py -- in.json out.json

WHY THIS EXISTS, and why it is not IK.

A KeyframeSequence is per-joint rotations, so the shipped spec must contain plain
FK angles - `anim_render.py` must never see a `target` or an `aim`. But some
angles are not guessable: "the support hand holds the rifle so the butt sits in
the shoulder pocket and the muzzle points down-range" is a statement about a
world FRAME, and hand-tuning nine angles against a render to satisfy it is the
expensive loop this skill exists to avoid.

So the solve happens HERE, ONCE, OFFLINE, and its output is frozen into the spec
as constants. The distinction that matters:

  * IK in the clip = a solver runs per frame, picks whichever branch it likes,
    leaves limb ROLL free, and pops between frames. That is banned.
  * a solver run once per BEAT, seeded from the previous beat, whose numbers are
    then written into the spec as plain `rot` values = FK. Interpolation between
    beats is in joint space, roll is fully determined (the frame objective pins
    it), and nothing is solved at render time.

It also derives a prop grip offset in BONE space from a desired WORLD placement,
which is "never type a grip" applied one level up: the placement is stated as a
fact about the scene ("butt at the right shoulder, barrel forward, sights up")
and the bone-space numbers are computed from the posed rig.
"""
import bpy, json, math, sys, os
from mathutils import Euler, Vector, Matrix

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
inp = json.load(open(argv[0]))
outpath = argv[1]

R15 = {"HumanoidRootPart", "LowerTorso", "UpperTorso", "Head",
       "LeftUpperArm", "LeftLowerArm", "LeftHand",
       "RightUpperArm", "RightLowerArm", "RightHand",
       "LeftUpperLeg", "LeftLowerLeg", "LeftFoot",
       "RightUpperLeg", "RightLowerLeg", "RightFoot"}


def die(msg):
    print(f"\n!!! FAILED: {msg}", flush=True)
    sys.stdout.flush()
    os._exit(1)


arm = None
for o in bpy.data.objects:
    if o.type == "ARMATURE" and len({b.name for b in o.data.bones} & R15) >= 10:
        arm = o
        break
if arm is None:
    die("no R15 armature")
M = arm.matrix_world
sc = bpy.context.scene
sc.frame_set(0)
bpy.context.view_layer.update()
ORIGIN = (M @ arm.pose.bones["HumanoidRootPart"].head).copy()
print(f"=== rig-space origin {tuple(round(v,3) for v in ORIGIN)}")

PROPS = inp.get("properties", {})
prop_bone = None
if PROPS:
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        if all(k in pb.keys() for k in PROPS):
            prop_bone = pb
            break
    if prop_bone is None:
        die(f"no pose bone carries all of {list(PROPS)}")

REST_ROT = {b.name: b.rotation_euler.copy() for b in arm.pose.bones}
REST_LOC = {b.name: b.location.copy() for b in arm.pose.bones}


def reset():
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        if pb.rotation_mode == "QUATERNION":
            pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
        pb.rotation_euler = REST_ROT[pb.name]
        pb.location = REST_LOC[pb.name]
    for k, v in PROPS.items():
        prop_bone[k] = v
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()


def apply(pose):
    for bone, spec in pose.items():
        if bone not in arm.pose.bones:
            die(f"unknown bone {bone!r}")
        pb = arm.pose.bones[bone]
        if "rot" in spec:
            if pb.rotation_mode == "QUATERNION":
                pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
            pb.rotation_euler = Euler([math.radians(v) for v in spec["rot"]], "XYZ")
        if "loc" in spec:
            pb.location = Vector(spec["loc"])
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()


def head(b):
    return M @ arm.pose.bones[b].head


def bone_frame(b):
    return M @ arm.pose.bones[b].matrix


def basis(x_dir, z_dir):
    xd = Vector(x_dir).normalized()
    zd = Vector(z_dir)
    zd = (zd - xd * zd.dot(xd)).normalized()
    yd = zd.cross(xd)
    return Matrix(((xd.x, yd.x, zd.x), (xd.y, yd.y, zd.y), (xd.z, yd.z, zd.z)))


def want_frame(spec):
    return Matrix.Translation(ORIGIN + Vector(spec["pos"])) @ basis(
        spec["x_dir"], spec["z_dir"]).to_4x4()


def set_params(params, vals):
    for (bone, axis), v in zip(params, vals):
        pb = arm.pose.bones[bone]
        if pb.rotation_mode == "QUATERNION":
            pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
        e = list(pb.rotation_euler)
        e[int(axis)] = math.radians(v)
        pb.rotation_euler = Euler(e, "XYZ")
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()


def gauss_solve(A, b):
    """Plain Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. mathutils.Matrix only
    inverts 2x2/3x3/4x4 and a nine-angle solve needs 9x9."""
    n = len(b)
    m = [row[:] + [b[i]] for i, row in enumerate(A)]
    for c in range(n):
        p = max(range(c, n), key=lambda r: abs(m[r][c]))
        if abs(m[p][c]) < 1e-12:
            return None
        m[c], m[p] = m[p], m[c]
        pv = m[c][c]
        for r in range(n):
            if r == c:
                continue
            f = m[r][c] / pv
            if f:
                for k in range(c, n + 1):
                    m[r][k] -= f * m[c][k]
    return [m[i][n] / m[i][i] for i in range(n)]


def rotvec(Ra, Rb):
    """Rotation vector taking Ra to Rb, in world axes (radians * axis)."""
    q = (Rb.to_3x3() @ Ra.to_3x3().transposed()).to_quaternion()
    ang = q.angle
    if ang > math.pi:
        ang -= 2 * math.pi
    ax = q.axis
    return ax * ang


def dls(params, seed, err_fn, iters=90, h=0.5, damp0=1.0, reg=2e-3, cap=20.0):
    """Damped least squares over joint ANGLES in degrees.

    `err_fn()` returns a list of residuals (position in studs, and for a frame
    objective the orientation residual pre-weighted into the same units). The
    seed is the previous beat's answer, which is what keeps consecutive beats on
    the same branch - the thing a per-frame IK solver does not give you."""
    x = list(seed)
    n = len(x)

    def E(v):
        set_params(params, v)
        return err_fn()

    def norm(e):
        return math.sqrt(sum(c * c for c in e))

    best = list(x)
    best_e = norm(E(x))
    lam = damp0
    for _ in range(iters):
        base = E(x)
        if norm(base) < 1e-4:
            break
        cols = []
        for i in range(n):
            p = list(x)
            p[i] += h
            ei = E(p)
            cols.append([(ei[k] - base[k]) / h for k in range(len(base))])
        A = [[sum(cols[i][k] * cols[j][k] for k in range(len(base)))
              + (lam + reg if i == j else 0.0) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
        rhs = [-sum(cols[i][k] * base[k] for k in range(len(base))) for i in range(n)]
        step = gauss_solve(A, rhs)
        if step is None:
            lam *= 10
            if lam > 1e7:
                break
            continue
        L = math.sqrt(sum(s * s for s in step))
        if L > cap:
            step = [s * cap / L for s in step]
        trial = [x[i] + step[i] for i in range(n)]
        te = norm(E(trial))
        if te < best_e:
            best, best_e, x = list(trial), te, trial
            lam = max(lam * 0.5, 1e-4)
        else:
            lam *= 4
            if lam > 1e7:
                break
    set_params(params, best)
    return best, best_e


GRIPS = {}
out = {"grips": {}, "beats": {}}

for q in inp["queries"]:
    reset()
    apply(q.get("pose", {}))
    rec = {"solved": {}, "residual": {}, "positions": {}, "landmarks": {}}

    def record(params, vals):
        for (bone, axis), v in zip(params, vals):
            rec["solved"].setdefault(bone, {})[str(int(axis))] = round(v, 3)

    for op in q.get("ops", []):
        kind = op["op"]
        if kind == "grip":
            Bm = bone_frame(op["attach"])
            off = Bm.inverted() @ want_frame(op)
            e = off.to_euler("XYZ")
            GRIPS[op["name"]] = {
                "attach": op["attach"],
                "pos": [round(v, 5) for v in off.translation],
                "rot": [round(math.degrees(v), 4) for v in e],
            }
            out["grips"][op["name"]] = GRIPS[op["name"]]
            print(f"=== grip {op['name']!r} on {op['attach']}: "
                  f"pos {GRIPS[op['name']]['pos']} rot {GRIPS[op['name']]['rot']}")
        elif kind == "frame_solve":
            g = GRIPS[op["grip"]]
            G = (Matrix.Translation(Vector(g["pos"]))
                 @ Euler([math.radians(v) for v in g["rot"]], "XYZ").to_matrix().to_4x4())
            T = want_frame(op)
            w = op.get("rot_weight", 0.55)
            params = [(b, a) for b, a in op["params"]]

            def err_fn(G=G, T=T, w=w, att=g["attach"]):
                P = bone_frame(att) @ G
                d = T.translation - P.translation
                rv = rotvec(P, T)
                return [d.x, d.y, d.z, rv.x * w, rv.y * w, rv.z * w]

            vals, res = dls(params, op["seed"], err_fn)
            record(params, vals)
            rec["residual"][op.get("name", op["grip"])] = round(res, 4)
        elif kind == "point_solve":
            tgt = op.get("target")
            if tgt is None:
                g = GRIPS[op["target_local"]["grip"]]
                G = (Matrix.Translation(Vector(g["pos"]))
                     @ Euler([math.radians(v) for v in g["rot"]], "XYZ").to_matrix().to_4x4())
                P = bone_frame(g["attach"]) @ G
                tgt = list((P @ Vector(op["target_local"]["local"])) - ORIGIN)
            params = [(b, a) for b, a in op["params"]]
            eff = op["effector"]

            def err_fn(tgt=tgt, eff=eff):
                d = Vector(tgt) - (head(eff) - ORIGIN)
                return [d.x, d.y, d.z]

            vals, res = dls(params, op["seed"], err_fn)
            record(params, vals)
            rec["residual"][eff] = round(res, 4)
            rec["landmarks"][eff + "_target"] = [round(v, 4) for v in tgt]
        elif kind == "report":
            for part in op["parts"]:
                v = head(part) - ORIGIN
                rec["positions"][part] = [round(v.x, 4), round(v.y, 4), round(v.z, 4)]
            for name, loc in op.get("prop_points", {}).items():
                g = GRIPS[op["grip"]]
                G = (Matrix.Translation(Vector(g["pos"]))
                     @ Euler([math.radians(v) for v in g["rot"]], "XYZ").to_matrix().to_4x4())
                P = bone_frame(g["attach"]) @ G
                v = (P @ Vector(loc)) - ORIGIN
                rec["landmarks"][name] = [round(v.x, 4), round(v.y, 4), round(v.z, 4)]
        else:
            die(f"unknown op {kind!r}")

    out["beats"][q["name"]] = rec
    bad = {k: v for k, v in rec["residual"].items() if v > q.get("tolerance", 0.05)}
    flag = f"  RESIDUAL HIGH {bad}" if bad else ""
    print(f"=== {q['name']}: residuals {rec['residual']}{flag}")

json.dump(out, open(outpath, "w"), indent=1)
print(f"=== wrote {outpath}")

"""Print the rest-pose frame of one bone, so a prop offset can be COMPUTED.

  blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python probe_bone.py -- RightHand

WHY. A prop offset that is guessed lands the weapon somewhere near the hand and
looks, in a contact sheet, exactly like a weapon that is somewhere near the hand.
The first attempt at this put a sword about two studs behind the fist and
the sheet was the only reason anybody knew.

The offset is not guessable because two different frames are in play:

  - Roblox positions a tool against the RightHand PART, whose axes are the
    character's (X right, Y up, Z back).
  - Blender parents to the RightHand BONE, whose +Y runs along the bone toward
    the fingertips and whose origin is the wrist.

They differ by a fixed rest transform, which this prints. Measure it once, put
the number in the spec, and the same contract grip then means the same thing in
both engines.
"""
import bpy
import sys
import math
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]

R15 = {"HumanoidRootPart", "LowerTorso", "UpperTorso", "Head",
       "LeftUpperArm", "LeftLowerArm", "LeftHand",
       "RightUpperArm", "RightLowerArm", "RightHand"}

arm = None
for o in bpy.data.objects:
    if o.type == "ARMATURE" and len({b.name for b in o.data.bones} & R15) >= 8:
        arm = o
        break
if arm is None:
    print("!!! FAILED: no R15 armature found")
    raise SystemExit(1)

bpy.context.view_layer.update()
M = arm.matrix_world

print(f"\n=== armature {arm.name!r} matrix_world translation {tuple(round(v,4) for v in M.translation)}")

pb = arm.pose.bones.get(want)
if pb is None:
    print(f"!!! FAILED: no bone {want!r}. Bones containing 'Hand': "
          f"{[b.name for b in arm.pose.bones if 'Hand' in b.name]}")
    raise SystemExit(1)

world = M @ pb.matrix
head = M @ pb.head
tail = M @ pb.tail
print(f"\n=== bone {want!r}")
print(f"  head (world)   {tuple(round(v,4) for v in head)}")
print(f"  tail (world)   {tuple(round(v,4) for v in tail)}")
print(f"  length         {round((tail-head).length,4)}")

print(f"    Y {tuple(round(v,4) for v in world.col[1][:3])}   <- along the bone")

# The character's own frame, so the offset can be expressed the way the game

root = arm.pose.bones.get("HumanoidRootPart")
if root:
    rw = M @ root.matrix
    print(f"\n=== HumanoidRootPart origin {tuple(round(v,4) for v in rw.translation)}")
    rel = rw.inverted() @ world
    print(f"  {want} relative to root:")
    print(f"    translation {tuple(round(v,4) for v in rel.translation)}")

    print(f"    rotation deg {tuple(round(math.degrees(v),2) for v in e)}")

# What a prop at offset (0,0,0) would inherit, spelled out, because that is the

print(f"\n=== a prop with grip pos [0,0,0] rot [0,0,0] lands at "
      f"{tuple(round(v,4) for v in world.translation)} "
      f"with its local +Y along {tuple(round(v,4) for v in world.col[1][:3])}")

"""R6 joint-space clip -> posed render of the rig's real mesh parts + numeric checks. No .blend needed.

  blender --background --python-exit-code 1 --python r6_clip.py -- --rig rig.json --glb-dir parts/ --clip clip.json \
      --outdir out/Clip [--hide PartGlbName] [--size 360] [--no-render]

WHY (2026-10-17): a custom-mesh R6 monster rig is (rigid GLB parts welded by
Motor6Ds in Studio) with no .blend, so anim_render.py has nothing to key. A KeyframeSequence
Pose.CFrame IS the Motor6D Transform (world(P1) = P0 * C0 * T * C1:Inverse()), so the clip is
authored in that space (semantic angles, see r6_joint.py) and VERIFIED here by applying exactly
that chain to the shipped meshes. Render and Luau read one conversion (r6_joint.transform).

rig.json: {"hrp": [x,y,z],
           "parts": {"Torso": {"glb": "MonsterTorso"}, ...},           # glb = file stem in --glb-dir
           "joints": [{"name": "RootJoint", "part0": "HumanoidRootPart", "part1": "Torso",
                       "c0": {"pos": [..], "rows": [[..],[..],[..]]}, "c1": {...}}, ...],
           "feet": ["Right Leg", "Left Leg"], "arms": ["Right Arm", "Left Arm"],
           "arm_check_below_y": 4.4}                                    # rest-y below which arm verts are "hands"
  Frame: Roblox studs, +Y up, -Z forward, +X right, feet at y=0. Every part rests UNROTATED at its
  mesh bbox centre (a MeshPart centres on its bbox); the script asserts the C0/C1 chain reproduces it.

clip.json: {"name", "fps": 30, "duration", "loop", "priority", "markers": [[name, t], ...],
            "auto_ground": false,
            "keyframes": [{"t", "ease", "ground": bool, "joints": {"RootJoint": {"pitch":..,"pos":[..]},
                                                                  "Right Shoulder": {"swing":..}, ...}}]}
  "ground": true on a key solves RootJoint pos.y so the lowest foot vertex sits at y=0 on that key.

Writes: frames side_###.png / tq_###.png, report.json (per-frame lowest foot y, per-leg lowest y and
contact-point slide speed, hand-vs-leg/torso triangle overlaps vs the rest baseline) and
resolved.json (Pose CFrames per key, consumed by r6_luau.py). Exits non-zero on any failed assertion.
Pass --python-exit-code 1: without it a Python exception in here still exits Blender with 0.
"""
import bpy, sys, os, json, math, glob, argparse
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector, Quaternion
from mathutils.bvhtree import BVHTree

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import r6_joint as RJ  # noqa: E402
import functools
# os._exit() below skips the stdout flush, which silently ate every report line once
print = functools.partial(print, flush=True)  # noqa: A001

A = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--rig", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--glb-dir", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--clip", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--outdir", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--hide", default="")
ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=360)
ap.add_argument("--no-render", action="store_true")
a = ap.parse_args(A)
outdir = os.path.abspath(a.outdir)
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)


def die(msg):
    print(f"\n!!! FAILED: {msg}", flush=True)
    os._exit(1)


rig = json.load(open(a.rig))
clip = json.load(open(a.clip))
FPS = clip.get("fps", 30)
DUR = clip["duration"]
LOOP = bool(clip.get("loop"))
KEYS = clip["keyframes"]
JOINTS = {j["name"]: j for j in rig["joints"]}
BY_CHILD = {j["part1"]: j for j in rig["joints"]}


def cf(d):
    m = Matrix([list(r) for r in d["rows"]]).to_4x4()
    m.translation = Vector(d["pos"])
    return m


# ---- rest CFrames from the chain, asserted against the mesh bboxes ----
REST = {"HumanoidRootPart": Matrix.Translation(Vector(rig["hrp"]))}
order = []
pending = list(rig["joints"])
while pending:
    for j in list(pending):
        if j["part0"] in REST:
            REST[j["part1"]] = REST[j["part0"]] @ cf(j["c0"]) @ cf(j["c1"]).inverted()
            order.append(j)
            pending.remove(j)
            break
    else:
        die("joint chain does not connect to HumanoidRootPart")

# ---- import meshes; Blender = Q * Roblox, Q:(X,Y,Z)->(-X,Z,Y) (glTF +Z-front file, Roblox front -Z) ----
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
Q = Matrix(((-1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0))).to_4x4()
QI = Q.inverted()
hidden = {h for h in a.hide.split(",") if h}
OBJ, VERTS, POLYS = {}, {}, {}
for pname, pd in rig["parts"].items():
    f = os.path.join(a.glb_dir, pd["glb"] + ".glb")
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        die(f"missing {f}")
    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=f)
    new = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o not in before]
    meshes = [o for o in new if o.type == "MESH"]
    if len(meshes) != 1:
        die(f"{f}: expected one mesh, got {len(meshes)}")
    o = meshes[0]
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    o.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = o
    o.parent = None
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=True, rotation=True, scale=True)
    for x in new:
        if x is not o:
            bpy.data.objects.remove(x, do_unlink=True)
    o.name = pname
    vb = np.array([tuple(v.co) for v in o.data.vertices])
    vr = vb @ np.array(QI.to_3x3()).T          # rest verts in Roblox frame
    VERTS[pname] = vr
    POLYS[pname] = [tuple(p.vertices) for p in o.data.polygons]
    c = (vr.min(0) + vr.max(0)) / 2
    err = (Vector(c) - REST[pname].translation).length
    print(f"=== {pname:10s} bbox centre {np.round(c, 3)}  chain rest {np.round(np.array(REST[pname].translation), 3)}  err {err:.4f}")
    if err > 0.03:
        die(f"{pname}: the C0/C1 chain puts the part {err:.3f} studs from its mesh bbox centre - wrong C0/C1 or frame")
    OBJ[pname] = o
for h in hidden:
    if h in bpy.data.objects:
        bpy.data.objects.remove(bpy.data.objects[h], do_unlink=True)


# ---- keyframes -> joint Transforms ----
keyed = set(KEYS[0]["joints"])
for k in KEYS:
    for jn, sem in k["joints"].items():
        if jn not in JOINTS:
            die(f"unknown joint {jn!r}")
        RJ.check_semantics(jn, sem)
    late = set(k["joints"]) - keyed
    if late:
        die(f"joints {sorted(late)} keyed at t={k['t']} but not in the first key")
if abs(KEYS[-1]["t"] - DUR) > 1e-6:
    die(f"last key t={KEYS[-1]['t']} != duration {DUR}")
if LOOP and json.dumps(KEYS[0]["joints"], sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(KEYS[-1]["joints"], sort_keys=True):
    die("loop clip: first and last keys differ - it would snap on every wrap")


def key_transforms(k):
    out = {}
    for jn in keyed:
        sem = k["joints"].get(jn, {})
        p, R = RJ.transform(JOINTS[jn], sem)
        m = Matrix(R).to_4x4()
        m.translation = Vector(p)
        out[jn] = m
    return out


def pose_world(T):
    W = {"HumanoidRootPart": REST["HumanoidRootPart"]}
    for j in order:
        t = T.get(j["name"], Matrix.Identity(4))
        W[j["part1"]] = W[j["part0"]] @ cf(j["c0"]) @ t @ cf(j["c1"]).inverted()
    return W


def posed_verts(W, p):
    M = W[p] @ REST[p].inverted()
    R = np.array(M.to_3x3())
    return VERTS[p] @ R.T + np.array(M.translation)


FEET = rig.get("feet", [])

# ground solve per key (RootJoint pos.y): lowest foot vertex -> y = 0
for k in KEYS:
    if k.get("ground") or (clip.get("auto_ground") and k.get("ground") is not False):
        rj = k["joints"].setdefault("RootJoint", {})
        pos = list(rj.get("pos", [0, 0, 0]))
        pos[1] = 0.0
        rj["pos"] = pos
        W = pose_world(key_transforms(k))
        low = min(posed_verts(W, f)[:, 1].min() for f in FEET)
        pos[1] = round(-low, 4)
        rj["pos"] = pos
KT = [key_transforms(k) for k in KEYS]


def sample(t):
    if t <= KEYS[0]["t"]:
        return KT[0]
    for i in range(len(KEYS) - 1):
        a0, a1 = KEYS[i]["t"], KEYS[i + 1]["t"]
        if a0 <= t <= a1:
            u = RJ.ease(KEYS[i].get("ease", "smooth"), (t - a0) / (a1 - a0) if a1 > a0 else 1.0)
            out = {}
            for jn in keyed:
                m0, m1 = KT[i][jn], KT[i + 1][jn]
                q = m0.to_quaternion().slerp(m1.to_quaternion(), u)   # Roblox slerps the CFrame
                m = q.to_matrix().to_4x4()
                m.translation = m0.translation.lerp(m1.translation, u)
                out[jn] = m
            return out
    return KT[-1]


n = int(round(DUR * FPS)) + (0 if LOOP else 1)
times = [i / FPS for i in range(n)]

# ---- checks ----
ARMS = rig.get("arms", [])
cut = rig.get("arm_check_below_y", 4.4)


def subset_polys(p, mask):
    return [pl for pl in POLYS[p] if all(mask[v] for v in pl)]


ARM_POLYS = {p: subset_polys(p, VERTS[p][:, 1] < cut) for p in ARMS}
TORSO_NAME = "Torso"


def overlaps(W):
    vs = {p: posed_verts(W, p) for p in ARMS + FEET + [TORSO_NAME]}
    trees = {p: BVHTree.FromPolygons([tuple(v) for v in vs[p]], POLYS[p] if p not in ARMS else ARM_POLYS[p])
             for p in vs}
    res = {}
    for arm_p in ARMS:
        for other in FEET + [TORSO_NAME]:
            res[f"{arm_p}~{other}"] = len(trees[arm_p].overlap(trees[other]))
    return res


base = overlaps(pose_world({}))
print(f"=== rest-pose hand/claw overlaps (baseline): {base}")
frames = []
LEGV = {f: [] for f in FEET}
for i, t in enumerate(times):
    W = pose_world(sample(t))
    rec = {"f": i, "t": round(t, 4), "legs": {}}
    for f in FEET:
        v = posed_verts(W, f)
        LEGV[f].append(v)
        lo = v[:, 1].min()
        sel = v[v[:, 1] < lo + 0.03]
        rec["legs"][f] = {"low_y": round(float(lo), 4), "contact_xz": [round(float(sel[:, 0].mean()), 4),
                                                                        round(float(sel[:, 2].mean()), 4)]}
    rec["lowest_foot_y"] = min(r["low_y"] for r in rec["legs"].values())
    rec["hands"] = {}
    for ap_ in ARMS:
        v = posed_verts(W, ap_)
        rv = VERTS[ap_][:, 1]
        tip = v[rv < rv.min() + 0.6]            # the claws: rest-lowest 0.6 studs of the arm
        rec["hands"][ap_] = {"claw_centre": [round(float(x), 3) for x in tip.mean(0)],
                             "low_y": round(float(v[:, 1].min()), 3)}
    ov = overlaps(W)
    rec["hand_overlaps"] = {k: v for k, v in ov.items() if v > base.get(k, 0)}
    frames.append(rec)

# STANCE SLIP, measured on the MATERIAL point in contact (the lowest vertex at frame i, followed
# to frame i+1). The lowest-point LOCATION is useless here: a rigid foot rolls heel -> toe, so the
# contact location jumps along the sole while nothing slips. For no skating that vertex must move
# backward (+Z) at the character's ground speed. Frames wrap for a loop.
slides = []
nf = len(times)
for f in FEET:
    for i in range(nf - (0 if LOOP else 1)):
        j = (i + 1) % nf
        v0, v1 = LEGV[f][i], LEGV[f][j]
        k = int(np.argmin(v0[:, 1]))
        if v0[k, 1] < 0.06 and v1[k, 1] < 0.06:
            slides.append(float((v1[k, 2] - v0[k, 2]) * FPS))
slide = {"samples": len(slides), "mean_backward_speed": round(float(np.mean(slides)), 3) if slides else None,
         "median": round(float(np.median(slides)), 3) if slides else None,
         "min": round(float(np.min(slides)), 3) if slides else None,
         "max": round(float(np.max(slides)), 3) if slides else None}
worst_ov = max((sum(fr["hand_overlaps"].values()) for fr in frames), default=0)
report = {"clip": clip["name"], "frames": len(frames), "baseline_overlaps": base,
          "lowest_foot_y_min": min(fr["lowest_foot_y"] for fr in frames),
          "lowest_foot_y_max": max(fr["lowest_foot_y"] for fr in frames),
          "stance_slide": slide,
          "lowest_hand_y": min(h["low_y"] for fr in frames for h in fr["hands"].values()), "worst_extra_hand_overlap_tris": worst_ov,
          "frames_with_hand_overlap": [fr["f"] for fr in frames if fr["hand_overlaps"]],
          "per_frame": frames}
json.dump(report, open(os.path.join(outdir, "report.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(f"=== lowest foot y over the clip: {report['lowest_foot_y_min']:.3f} .. {report['lowest_foot_y_max']:.3f}")
print(f"=== stance contact slide (studs/s, +=backward): {slide}")
print(f"=== frames with NEW hand/claw overlaps: {report['frames_with_hand_overlap']} (worst {worst_ov} tri pairs)")

# resolved keys for the Luau builder
res = {"name": clip["name"], "priority": clip.get("priority", "Action"), "loop": LOOP, "duration": DUR,
       "markers": clip.get("markers", []), "keyed": sorted(keyed),
       "keys": [{"t": k["t"], "ease": k.get("ease", "smooth"),
                 "poses": {jn: {"pos": [round(x, 5) for x in KT[i][jn].translation],
                                "rows": [[round(KT[i][jn][r][c], 6) for c in range(3)] for r in range(3)]}
                           for jn in sorted(keyed)}} for i, k in enumerate(KEYS)]}
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(outdir, "resolved.json"), "w"), indent=1)

if a.no_render:
    print("=== no render requested")
    os._exit(0)

# ---- render: plain clay, floor at y=0, orthographic, framed on the whole clip ----
sc = bpy.context.scene
engines = {item.identifier for item in sc.render.bl_rna.properties["engine"].enum_items}
if "BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT" in engines:
    sc.render.engine = "BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT"
elif "BLENDER_EEVEE" in engines:
    sc.render.engine = "BLENDER_EEVEE"
else:
    die("no supported Eevee renderer in this Blender build")
sc.render.resolution_x = sc.render.resolution_y = a.size
sc.view_settings.view_transform = "Standard"
world = bpy.data.worlds.new("W")
sc.world = world
world.use_nodes = True
world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[0].default_value = (0.42, 0.45, 0.5, 1)
world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[1].default_value = 0.6


def mat(name, col):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*col, 1)
    b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.7
    return m


COL = {"Torso": (0.16, 0.16, 0.18), "Head": (0.75, 0.62, 0.42)}
for p, o in OBJ.items():
    if o.name not in bpy.data.objects:
        continue
    o.data.materials.clear()
    o.data.materials.append(mat(p + "_m", COL.get(p, (0.72, 0.74, 0.70))))
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=60)
fl = bpy.context.active_object
fl.data.materials.append(mat("floor", (0.25, 0.27, 0.25)))
sun = bpy.data.objects.new("sun", bpy.data.lights.new("sun", "SUN"))
sun.data.energy = 3.5
sun.rotation_euler = (math.radians(50), math.radians(10), math.radians(-35))
sc.collection.objects.link(sun)

poses = [pose_world(sample(t)) for t in times]
pts = []
for W in poses:
    for p in OBJ:
        if OBJ[p].name in bpy.data.objects:
            v = posed_verts(W, p)
            pts += [v.min(0), v.max(0)]
pts = np.array(pts)
lo, hi = pts.min(0), pts.max(0)
lo[1] = min(lo[1], 0.0)
ctr = (lo + hi) / 2
ext = float((hi - lo).max()) * 1.12
# view dirs in Roblox frame (from target to camera): side = character's right, tq = front-right
VIEWS = {"side": (1.0, 0.0, 0.0), "tq": (0.75, 0.25, -0.75)}
cam = bpy.data.objects.new("cam", bpy.data.cameras.new("cam"))
sc.collection.objects.link(cam)
sc.camera = cam
cam.data.type = "ORTHO"
cam.data.ortho_scale = ext
for vn, d in VIEWS.items():
    dv = Vector(d).normalized()
    c_r = Vector(ctr.tolist())
    pos_r = c_r + dv * 40
    cam.location = Q.to_3x3() @ pos_r
    cam.rotation_euler = (Q.to_3x3() @ (c_r - pos_r)).to_track_quat("-Z", "Y").to_euler()
    for i, W in enumerate(poses):
        for p, o in OBJ.items():
            if o.name in bpy.data.objects:
                o.matrix_world = Q @ (W[p] @ REST[p].inverted()) @ QI
        sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(outdir, f"{vn}_{i:03d}.png")
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
missing = [f for vn in VIEWS for f in (os.path.join(outdir, f"{vn}_{i:03d}.png") for i in range(n)) if not os.path.exists(f)]
if missing:
    die(f"{len(missing)} frames not written, e.g. {missing[0]}")
print(f"=== done: {n} frames x {len(VIEWS)} views -> {outdir}")
os._exit(0)

"""R6 joint-space clip maths, pure Python (no bpy): semantic angles -> Motor6D Transform CFrames.

Shared by r6_clip.py (the Blender renderer/verifier) and r6_luau.py (the KeyframeSequence
builder), so the render and the game read ONE conversion and cannot drift apart.

WHY (2026-10-17): a custom-mesh R6 monster rig is (rigid GLB parts,
Motor6Ds built in Studio) with NO .blend, so anim_render.py's FK-bone route does not
exist for it. A KeyframeSequence Pose.CFrame IS the Motor6D Transform:
    world(Part1) = Part0.CFrame * C0 * Transform * C1:Inverse()
so clips are authored straight in that space, from the probed C0/C1.

SEMANTIC ANGLES (degrees), all measured in the PARENT part's rest axes, Roblox frame
(+X character right, +Y up, -Z forward):
  up-pointing joints (RootJoint, Neck - the child sits ABOVE the pivot):
    pitch  + = top tips FORWARD (bow)      lean + = top tips to the character's LEFT
    turn   + = face turns LEFT (about up)
  limb joints (Shoulders, Hips - the child hangs BELOW the pivot):
    swing  + = limb swings FORWARD          spread + = limb swings OUTWARD (away from body)
    twist  + = about the up axis (limb front face turns left)
  pos = [dx, dy, dz] studs, parent-frame offset of the child (RootJoint bob).
World rotation W = Ry(turn|twist) * Rz(lean|+-spread) * Rx(-pitch|+swing); the Transform is
T = R0^T W R0 with R0 the C0 rotation, so W is a rotation about the joint point in the
parent's axes regardless of how C0 happens to be oriented. Which side a limb is on is read
from C0's position (x > 0 = right), never from a mirror rule.

Note what a torso pitch does to its children: pitching the torso forward swings hanging
arms and legs BACKWARD (their bottoms move back); compensate in the child joints.
"""
import math

UP_JOINTS = {"RootJoint", "Neck"}


def rx(a):
    c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
    return [[1, 0, 0], [0, c, -s], [0, s, c]]


def ry(a):
    c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
    return [[c, 0, s], [0, 1, 0], [-s, 0, c]]


def rz(a):
    c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
    return [[c, -s, 0], [s, c, 0], [0, 0, 1]]


def mm(a, b):
    return [[sum(a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(3)) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]


def tr(a):
    return [[a[j][i] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]


def mv(a, v):
    return [sum(a[i][k] * v[k] for k in range(3)) for i in range(3)]


def world_rot(joint_name, side_sign, sem):
    """Semantic dict -> W (3x3), rotation in the parent's rest axes."""
    d = math.radians
    if joint_name in UP_JOINTS:
        a = d(-sem.get("pitch", 0.0))
        b = d(sem.get("lean", 0.0))
        c = d(sem.get("turn", 0.0))
    else:
        a = d(sem.get("swing", 0.0))
        b = d(sem.get("spread", 0.0)) * side_sign
        c = d(sem.get("twist", 0.0))
    return mm(ry(c), mm(rz(b), rx(a)))


def transform(joint, sem):
    """joint = {"name", "c0": {"pos", "rows"}} ; returns (pos[3], rows[3][3]) of the Pose CFrame."""
    R0 = joint["c0"]["rows"]
    side = 1.0 if joint["c0"]["pos"][0] >= 0 else -1.0
    W = world_rot(joint["name"], side, sem)
    T = mm(tr(R0), mm(W, R0))
    p = sem.get("pos", [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    tp = mv(tr(R0), p)
    return tp, T


def check_semantics(joint_name, sem):
    allowed = {"pitch", "lean", "turn", "pos"} if joint_name in UP_JOINTS else {"swing", "spread", "twist", "pos"}
    bad = set(sem) - allowed
    if bad:
        raise SystemExit(f"{joint_name}: unknown semantic keys {sorted(bad)}; allowed {sorted(allowed)}")


def ease(name, u):
    if name == "linear":
        return u
    if name == "constant":
        return 0.0
    if name == "in":      # accelerate INTO the next key (Roblox PoseEasingDirection.Out - reversed enum)
        return u ** 3
    if name == "out":     # decelerate into the next key (Roblox PoseEasingDirection.In)
        return 1 - (1 - u) ** 3
    if name == "smooth":
        return 4 * u ** 3 if u < 0.5 else 1 - (-2 * u + 2) ** 3 / 2
    raise SystemExit(f"unknown ease {name!r}")


# spec ease -> (Enum.PoseEasingStyle, Enum.PoseEasingDirection). Direction In/Out are BACKWARDS
# in Roblox's Pose enum (docs: "for legacy compatibility reasons"), see traps.md #36.
ROBLOX_EASE = {"linear": ("Linear", "In"), "constant": ("Constant", "In"),
               "in": ("Cubic", "Out"), "out": ("Cubic", "In"), "smooth": ("Cubic", "InOut")}

with to_roblox.convert() so both rigs land in one script under one replaced-wholesale folder.

  * the target folder is DESTROYED and rebuilt (it is a place-side generated folder; nothing else

def n(v):
    s = ("%.5f" % v).rstrip("0").rstrip(".")

def r6_clip_lua(res):
    times = [k["t"] for k in res["keys"]]
    rows = []
    mk_at = {}
    for name, t in res.get("markers", []):
        hit = [i for i, kt in enumerate(times) if abs(kt - t) < 1e-4]
        if not hit:
            raise SystemExit(f"{res['name']}: marker {name}@{t} is not on a keyframe")
        mk_at.setdefault(hit[0], []).append(name)
    for i, k in enumerate(res["keys"]):
        style, direction = RJ.ROBLOX_EASE[k["ease"]]
        ps = []
        for jn, pc in sorted(k["poses"].items()):
            part = R6_JOINT_TO_PART[jn]
            vals = list(pc["pos"]) + [x for r in pc["rows"] for x in r]
            ps.append('["%s"]={c={%s}}' % (part, ",".join(n(v) for v in vals)))
        m = ',m={%s}' % ",".join('"%s"' % x for x in mk_at[i]) if i in mk_at else ""
        rows.append('{t=%s,s="%s",d="%s",poses={%s}%s}' % (n(k["t"]), style, direction, ",".join(ps), m))
    return res["name"], res["priority"], res["loop"], "{" + ",".join(rows) + "}"


def r15_clip_lua(path):
    import to_roblox
    d = to_roblox.convert(path)
    rows = []
    for k in d["keyframes"]:
        ps = []
        for j, v in sorted(k["poses"].items()):
            bits = []
            if "r" in v:
                bits.append("r={%s}" % ",".join(n(x) for x in v["r"]))
            if "p" in v:
                bits.append("p={%s}" % ",".join(n(x) for x in v["p"]))
            ps.append('["%s"]={%s}' % (j, ",".join(bits)))
        ms = [m for m, t in d["markers"].items() if abs(t - k["t"]) < 1e-6]
        mk = ",m={%s}" % ",".join('"%s"' % m for m in sorted(ms)) if ms else ""
        rows.append('{t=%s,s="%s",d="%s",poses={%s}%s}' % (n(k["t"]), k["s"], k["d"], ",".join(ps), mk))
    return d["name"], d["priority"], d["loop"], "{" + ",".join(rows) + "}"

def lua_tree(tree):
    return "{" + ",".join('{"%s","%s"}' % (c, p) for c, p in tree) + "}"


def builder(folder, r6_paths, r15_paths, r6_sub="R6", r15_sub="R15"):
    import to_roblox
    segs = folder.split(".")
    if segs[0] == "ReplicatedStorage":
        segs = segs[1:]
    if not segs:
        raise SystemExit("--folder must name a folder under ReplicatedStorage")
    out = [HEAD % {"folder": folder, "r15tree": lua_tree(to_roblox.TREE), "r6tree": lua_tree(R6_TREE),
                   "segs": "{" + ",".join('"%s"' % s for s in segs) + "}"}]
    for p in r15_paths:
        name, pr, lp, kfs = r15_clip_lua(p)
        out.append('add("R15","%s","%s","%s",%s,%s)' % (r15_sub, name, pr, str(lp).lower(), kfs))
    for p in r6_paths:

        out.append('add("R6","%s","%s","%s",%s,%s)' % (r6_sub, name, pr, str(lp).lower(), kfs))

"""Does the Roblox KeyframeSequence pose the part the way Blender rendered it?

  blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python rbx_axis_check.py -- spec.json [spec2.json ...]

THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS FOR (found 2026-10-08):
to_roblox.py converted every FK bone with one rule, rx=-bx ry=by rz=bz. Probing
the community R15 rig showed that rule is only right for X and Z on the LIMBS:

  * limb bones point DOWN, so their local frame is the Roblox frame turned 180
    degrees about Z. That makes ry = -by, not +by: Blender FK_UpperArm.R Y=+90
    swings the elbow BACKWARD, Roblox Ry(+90) on RightShoulder swings it FORWARD.
    Any arm roll (cocked throw, hand on hip) came out mirrored in game.
  * torso/head bones point UP and share Roblox's frame, so their map is the
    identity. UpTorso X=+20 leans the head BACK in Blender (measured, head tip
    y -0.89); Roblox Rx(+) on the Waist also leans back - but the old rule sent
    -20, so every authored lean played the OTHER way in game.

The contact sheet cannot see this: it only proves the render matches the spec.
Studio was the only place it would show, and only if someone compared.

WHAT IT DOES: for every authored beat it poses the Blender rig exactly as the
spec says, reads each deform part's world rotation (delta from rest), and
compares it with the rotation Roblox will compute from to_roblox.convert()'s
numbers - composed down the Motor6D chain as Pose CFrames
(CFrame.Angles(0,0,rz)*CFrame.Angles(0,ry,0)*CFrame.Angles(rx,0,0)), assuming
R15 rig attachments are axis-aligned (true for the stock R15 rig). Full
rotation, so ROLL is checked as well as direction. Prints the worst error per
part and exits non-zero if any part is off by more than --tol degrees (2.0).

--mid adds the segment-midpoint comparison (Euler lerp vs CFrame slerp), which
is a REPORT, not a gate: it says where the in-game path will leave the render's.

It must be able to FAIL: run it with --legacy to use the old rule and it should
report the torso/limb-roll errors. A checker that cannot fail proves nothing.
"""
import bpy, sys, os, json, math, argparse
from mathutils import Euler, Matrix, Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("specs", nargs="+")
# 2.0, not 0: the community R15 rig's FK limb bones are built slightly off-axis (measured
# from the bone matrices: upper arms 0.74 deg, lower arms 0.49 deg, upper legs
# 0.68 deg), so a perfect conversion still leaves ~1.4 deg at 150 deg of swing.
# The defect this hunts is 12-170 deg. Do not raise this to pass a spec.
ap.add_argument("--tol", type=float, default=2.0, help="max allowed rotation error, degrees")
ap.add_argument("--mid", action="store_true",
                help="also compare the MIDPOINT of every segment: Blender lerps Euler angles, "
                     "Roblox slerps CFrames, so a big multi-axis move can take a different PATH "
                     "in game than in the render even when every key matches")
ap.add_argument("--legacy", action="store_true", help="use the pre-2026-10-08 axis rule (should FAIL)")
args = ap.parse_args(argv)

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import to_roblox  # noqa: E402

TREE = dict(to_roblox.TREE)  # child -> parent
R15 = set(TREE) | {"HumanoidRootPart"}


def die(msg):
    print(f"\n!!! FAILED: {msg}", flush=True)
    os._exit(1)


arm = next((o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE"
            and len({b.name for b in o.data.bones} & R15) >= 12), None)
if arm is None:
    die("no R15 armature")
M = arm.matrix_world
sc = bpy.context.scene
act = arm.animation_data.action if arm.animation_data else None
if act is None:
    die("rig has no action to key into (see traps #1)")

# world -> Roblox: world +X right, +Y forward, +Z up  ->  Roblox +X right, +Y up, -Z forward
P = Matrix(((1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), (0, -1, 0)))


def world_rot(b):
    return (M @ arm.pose.bones[b].matrix).to_3x3().normalized()


def cf(r):
    rx, ry, rz = (math.radians(v) for v in r)
    return Matrix.Rotation(rz, 3, "Z") @ Matrix.Rotation(ry, 3, "Y") @ Matrix.Rotation(rx, 3, "X")


sc.frame_set(0)
bpy.context.view_layer.update()
REST = {b: world_rot(b) for b in TREE}
frame = 2000
worst_all = 0.0
for path in args.specs:
    spec = json.load(open(path))
    conv = to_roblox.convert(path, legacy=args.legacy)
    props = spec.get("properties", {})
    pbp = next((pb for pb in arm.pose.bones if props and all(k in pb.keys() for k in props)), None)
    bones = sorted({b for k in spec["keyframes"] for b in k["bones"]})
    worst = {}
    def pose_compare(bl_rot, rb_rot, locs):
        """bl_rot: {bone: euler deg}; rb_rot: {joint: 3x3 local rotation}. Returns {part: err}."""
        global frame
        frame += 5
        sc.frame_set(frame)
        for p, v in props.items():
            pbp[p] = v
            pbp.keyframe_insert(f'["{p}"]', frame=frame)
        for b in bones:
            pb = arm.pose.bones[b]
            if pb.rotation_mode == "QUATERNION":
                pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
            pb.rotation_euler = Euler([math.radians(v) for v in bl_rot.get(b, (0, 0, 0))], "XYZ")
            pb.keyframe_insert("rotation_euler", frame=frame)
            if b in locs:
                pb.location = Vector(locs[b])
                pb.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        sc.frame_set(frame)
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        rbx_world = {"HumanoidRootPart": Matrix.Identity(3)}
        for child, parent in to_roblox.TREE:  # parents precede children
            rbx_world[child] = rbx_world[parent] @ rb_rot.get(child, Matrix.Identity(3))
        errs = {}
        for part in TREE:
            d_bl = world_rot(part) @ REST[part].inverted()
            d_bl = P @ d_bl @ P.transposed()
            e = math.degrees((rbx_world[part].transposed() @ d_bl).to_quaternion().angle)
            errs[part] = min(e, 360 - e)
        return errs

    def bl_of(k):
        return {b: d.get("rot", (0, 0, 0)) for b, d in k["bones"].items()}

    def rb_of(ck):
        return {j: cf(v.get("r", (0, 0, 0))) for j, v in ck["poses"].items()}

    def locs_of(k):
        return {b: d["loc"] for b, d in k["bones"].items() if "loc" in d}

    for k, ck in zip(spec["keyframes"], conv["keyframes"]):
        for part, err in pose_compare(bl_of(k), rb_of(ck), locs_of(k)).items():
            if err > worst.get(part, (0, 0))[0]:
                worst[part] = (err, k["t"])
    if args.mid:
        mids = []
        K, C = spec["keyframes"], conv["keyframes"]
        for a, b, ca, cb in zip(K, K[1:], C, C[1:]):
            ba, bb = bl_of(a), bl_of(b)
            bl_mid = {n: [(x + y) / 2 for x, y in zip(ba.get(n, (0, 0, 0)), bb.get(n, (0, 0, 0)))]
                      for n in set(ba) | set(bb)}
            ra, rbb = rb_of(ca), rb_of(cb)
            rb_mid = {}
            for j in set(ra) | set(rbb):
                qa = ra.get(j, Matrix.Identity(3)).to_quaternion()
                qb = rbb.get(j, Matrix.Identity(3)).to_quaternion()
                rb_mid[j] = qa.slerp(qb, 0.5).to_matrix()
                # (mathutils slerp takes the short arc, as CFrame:Lerp does)
            la, lb = locs_of(a), locs_of(b)
            lm = {n: [(x + y) / 2 for x, y in zip(la[n], lb[n])] for n in la if n in lb}
            errs = pose_compare(bl_mid, rb_mid, lm)
            part = max(errs, key=errs.get)
            mids.append((errs[part], part, a["t"], b["t"]))
            if errs[part] > 10:
                # The cure is a beat AT the midpoint holding the pose Roblox will
                # actually pass through, so the render shows the in-game path.
                # Roblox local rotation -> Blender Euler: limbs conjugate by
                # C = diag(-1,-1,1) (180 deg about Z), body bones are the identity.
                Cm = Matrix(((-1, 0, 0), (0, -1, 0), (0, 0, 1)))
                inv = {v: k for k, v in to_roblox.JOINT.items()}
                sug = {}
                for j, R in sorted(rb_mid.items()):
                    bn = inv.get(j)
                    if bn is None:
                        continue
                    Rb = R if bn in to_roblox.BODY else Cm @ R @ Cm
                    sug[bn] = [round(math.degrees(v), 1) for v in Rb.to_euler("XYZ")]

"""Learn a control bone's AXIS CONVENTION and its USABLE RANGE.

  blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python sweep_control.py \
      -- IK_LEG.R:loc TORSO:rot ...

`calibrate_rig.py` tells you WHICH controls work. This tells you WHAT THEY DO:
for each axis it sweeps a range of values and reports where the driven deform
parts end up (in rig space, relative to the body root) plus whether the joints
stayed rigid at that magnitude.

Why this exists: axis conventions are per-bone and per-rig, and guessing them
costs whole authoring passes (a punch's twist authored on the lean axis hunched
the figure sideways for four passes). Just as important, IK controls have a
RANGE - push an IK target past the chain's reach and the limb stretches, which
the integrity assertion then rejects at render time. Reading the last magnitude
still marked `ok` tells you the budget BEFORE you author to it.

Output columns:
  value   the value written to that axis (degrees for rot, units for loc)
  <part>  that deform part's head position relative to the body root part, then
          how far the bone has TURNED from rest in degrees (`0d` = pure
          translation, a non-zero turn with an unchanged position = pure rotation
          about that joint, which is what foot and hand orientation controls do)
  drift   worst joint-length change vs rest; `TEAR` once it exceeds tolerance
"""
import bpy, math, sys
from mathutils import Euler, Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
if not argv:
    raise SystemExit("usage: -- BONE:mode [BONE:mode ...]   (mode = rot | loc)")

R15_CHAIN = {"LowerTorso": "HumanoidRootPart", "UpperTorso": "LowerTorso", "Head": "UpperTorso",
             "LeftUpperArm": "UpperTorso", "LeftLowerArm": "LeftUpperArm", "LeftHand": "LeftLowerArm",
             "RightUpperArm": "UpperTorso", "RightLowerArm": "RightUpperArm", "RightHand": "RightLowerArm",
             "LeftUpperLeg": "LowerTorso", "LeftLowerLeg": "LeftUpperLeg", "LeftFoot": "LeftLowerLeg",
             "RightUpperLeg": "LowerTorso", "RightLowerLeg": "RightUpperLeg", "RightFoot": "RightLowerLeg"}
R6_CHAIN = {}

arm = None
for o in bpy.data.objects:
    if o.type == "ARMATURE" and len({b.name for b in o.data.bones} & set(R15_CHAIN)) >= 10:
        arm = o
        break
if arm is None:
    raise SystemExit("no R15 armature found")
CHAIN = {c: p for c, p in R15_CHAIN.items() if c in arm.pose.bones and p in arm.pose.bones}
ROOTPART = "HumanoidRootPart" if "HumanoidRootPart" in arm.pose.bones else "LowerTorso"
M = arm.matrix_world
TOL = 0.06          # same tolerance anim_render.py asserts with


def head(b):
    return M @ arm.pose.bones[b].head


def lengths():
    return {c: (head(c) - head(p)).length for c, p in CHAIN.items()}


def rel(b):
    return head(b) - head(ROOTPART)


def direction(b):
    """Unit vector along the bone. MUST be measured alongside head position:
    a control that only ROTATES an end bone (a foot about its ankle, a hand
    about its wrist) moves no head at all, so a position-only probe declares it
    INERT and the axis never gets learned."""
    pb = arm.pose.bones[b]
    v = (M @ pb.tail) - (M @ pb.head)
    return v.normalized() if v.length > 1e-9 else Vector((0, 0, 1))


def angle_between(a, b):
    return math.degrees(math.acos(max(-1.0, min(1.0, a.dot(b)))))


BASE = {n: (arm.pose.bones[n].rotation_euler.copy(), arm.pose.bones[n].location.copy())
        for n in [pb.name for pb in arm.pose.bones]}


def restore():
    for n, (r, l) in BASE.items():
        pb = arm.pose.bones[n]
        pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
        pb.rotation_euler = r
        pb.location = l
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()


restore()
REST = lengths()
REST_POS = {b: rel(b).copy() for b in CHAIN}
REST_DIR = {b: direction(b).copy() for b in CHAIN}
print("=" * 78)
print(f"REST positions (relative to {ROOTPART}):")
for b in sorted(REST_POS):
    p = REST_POS[b]
    print(f"  {b:16s} ({p.x:+.2f}, {p.y:+.2f}, {p.z:+.2f})   len-to-parent {REST[b]:.3f}")

ROT_VALUES = [-90, -60, -35, -15, 15, 35, 60, 90]
LOC_VALUES = [-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, -0.25, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5]

for spec in argv:
    bone, _, mode = spec.partition(":")
    mode = mode or "rot"
    if bone not in arm.pose.bones:
        print(f"\n!! unknown bone {bone!r} - skipped")
        continue
    # which parts does this control actually drive? (measured, not assumed)
    restore()
    pb = arm.pose.bones[bone]
    pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
    if mode == "rot":
        pb.rotation_euler = Euler((0, 0, math.radians(35)), "XYZ")
    else:
        pb.location = Vector((0, 0, 0.5))
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    driven = [b for b in CHAIN
              if (rel(b) - REST_POS[b]).length > 0.02
              or angle_between(direction(b), REST_DIR[b]) > 2.0]
    if not driven:
        print(f"\n{'=' * 78}\n{bone}:{mode}  -- INERT, drives nothing. Do not author to it.")
        continue
    driven = driven[:3]

    print(f"\n{'=' * 78}\n{bone}:{mode}   drives: {', '.join(driven)}")
    vals = ROT_VALUES if mode == "rot" else LOC_VALUES
    for ax, axname in enumerate("XYZ"):
        print(f"\n  --- {axname} axis ---")
        hdr = "   value  " + "  ".join(f"{b[:14]:>28s}" for b in driven) + "   drift"
        print(hdr)
        for v in vals:
            restore()
            pb = arm.pose.bones[bone]
            pb.rotation_mode = "XYZ"
            if mode == "rot":
                e = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
                e[ax] = math.radians(v)
                pb.rotation_euler = Euler(e, "XYZ")
            else:
                l = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
                l[ax] = v
                pb.location = Vector(l)
            bpy.context.view_layer.update()
            now = lengths()
            limb = [b for b in REST if b != "LowerTorso"]
            drift = max(abs(now[b] - REST[b]) for b in limb)
            cells = []
            for b in driven:
                p = rel(b)
                turn = angle_between(direction(b), REST_DIR[b])
                cells.append(f"({p.x:+.2f},{p.y:+.2f},{p.z:+.2f}) {turn:3.0f}d".rjust(28))
            flag = "TEAR" if drift > TOL else "ok"
            print(f"   {v:+7.2f}  " + "  ".join(cells) + f"   {drift:.3f} {flag}")

restore()
print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("Read off: which axis moves the part the way you want, at what magnitude,")
print("and the LAST value still marked `ok` - that is your authoring budget.")

"""FK anim spec -> a ready-to-run Luau script that builds the KeyframeSequences in Studio.

  python to_roblox.py kick.json punch.json > build_sequences.lua
  python to_roblox.py a.json b.json --folder ReplicatedStorage.MyGame.Animations --no-verify > build.luau

Paste the output into `execute_luau`. It creates the target folder (default
ReplicatedStorage.CustomAnims, intermediate folders created as needed) holding
one KeyframeSequence per spec, replacing any child of the same name.

  --no-verify   emit a builder with NO yields: it skips the register-and-load
                check (which waits on AnimationTrack.Length) and instead returns
                a summary string built from the sequences it just made - per
                clip: keyframes, length, markers, joints posed. Use this when the
                caller needs execute_luau to return its output.

SPEC FIELDS READ: rbx_name, priority (default Action), loop, duration,
keyframes[], pose_only (contract: Roblox joint names the clip may pose),
markers {name: seconds} (each must coincide with an authored keyframe time;
emitted as KeyframeMarkers on that Keyframe, for GetMarkerReachedSignal).

AXIS MAP - corrected 2026-10-08 (see rbx_axis_check.py, which proves it):
  Roblox: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward. Pose CFrames are built in Blender's Euler
  order, CFrame.Angles(0,0,rz)*CFrame.Angles(0,ry,0)*CFrame.Angles(rx,0,0).
  LIMB bones (FK_UpperArm/LowerArm/Hand, FK_UpperLeg/LowerLeg/Foot) point DOWN;
  their local frame is Roblox's turned 180 degrees about Z, so
        rx = -bx    ry = -by    rz = bz
  BODY bones (TORSO, UpTorso, HEAD) point UP and share Roblox's frame, so
        rx = bx     ry = by     rz = bz
  The pre-2026-10-08 rule (rx=-bx ry=by rz=bz for everything) mirrored every
  limb ROLL and inverted every torso/head LEAN in game, while the Blender
  renders looked right. `--legacy-axes` reproduces it, for rbx_axis_check only.
  Translation (ROOT loc): Blender world (x, y fwd, z up) -> Roblox (x, z, -y).

EASING - corrected 2026-10-08: Enum.PoseEasingDirection In/Out are BACKWARDS
relative to TweenService and every other tool (Roblox docs, "for legacy
compatibility reasons"): PoseEasingDirection.Out applies the curve forward
(slow start, accelerate) and .In is the reversed curve (decelerate into the next
key). The old map sent the spec's "in" (accelerate into the strike) to .In, so
every strike DECELERATED into its contact frame in game - exactly the mushiness
the per-segment ease exists to prevent. Spec "in" -> Out, "out" -> In now.
"""
import argparse, json, sys, os

JOINT = {
    "TORSO": "LowerTorso", "UpTorso": "UpperTorso", "HEAD": "Head",
    "FK_UpperArm.R": "RightUpperArm", "FK_LowerArm.R": "RightLowerArm", "FK_Hand.R": "RightHand",
    "FK_UpperArm.L": "LeftUpperArm",  "FK_LowerArm.L": "LeftLowerArm",  "FK_Hand.L": "LeftHand",
    "FK_UpperLeg.R": "RightUpperLeg", "FK_LowerLeg.R": "RightLowerLeg", "FK_Foot.R": "RightFoot",
    "FK_UpperLeg.L": "LeftUpperLeg",  "FK_LowerLeg.L": "LeftLowerLeg",  "FK_Foot.L": "LeftFoot",
}
BODY = {"TORSO", "UpTorso", "HEAD"}
TREE = [("LowerTorso", "HumanoidRootPart"), ("UpperTorso", "LowerTorso"), ("Head", "UpperTorso"),
        ("LeftUpperArm", "UpperTorso"), ("LeftLowerArm", "LeftUpperArm"), ("LeftHand", "LeftLowerArm"),
        ("RightUpperArm", "UpperTorso"), ("RightLowerArm", "RightUpperArm"), ("RightHand", "RightLowerArm"),
        ("LeftUpperLeg", "LowerTorso"), ("LeftLowerLeg", "LeftUpperLeg"), ("LeftFoot", "LeftLowerLeg"),
        ("RightUpperLeg", "LowerTorso"), ("RightLowerLeg", "RightUpperLeg"), ("RightFoot", "RightLowerLeg")]
# Enum.PoseEasingStyle is Linear/Constant/Cubic/Elastic/Bounce - there is NO Quad.
# Enum.PoseEasingDirection In/Out are REVERSED vs TweenService (see docstring).
EASE = {"in": ("Cubic", "Out"), "out": ("Cubic", "In"),
        "smooth": ("Cubic", "InOut"), "linear": ("Linear", "In")}
EASE_LEGACY = {"in": ("Cubic", "In"), "out": ("Cubic", "Out"),
               "smooth": ("Cubic", "InOut"), "linear": ("Linear", "In")}


def map_rot(bone, r, legacy=False):
    bx, by, bz = r
    if legacy:
        return [-bx, by, bz]
    if bone in BODY:
        return [bx, by, bz]
    return [-bx, -by, bz]


def convert(path, legacy=False):
    spec = json.load(open(path))
    out = []
    ease = EASE_LEGACY if legacy else EASE
    for k in spec["keyframes"]:
        style, direction = ease[k.get("ease", "smooth")]
        poses = {}
        for bone, data in k["bones"].items():
            j = JOINT.get(bone)
            if j and "rot" in data:
                poses.setdefault(j, {})["r"] = map_rot(bone, data["rot"], legacy)
            if bone == "ROOT" and "loc" in data:
                lx, ly, lz = data["loc"]
                poses.setdefault("LowerTorso", {})["p"] = [lx, lz, -ly]
        out.append({"t": k["t"], "s": style, "d": direction, "poses": poses})
    name = spec.get("rbx_name") or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
    posed = sorted({j for k in out for j in k["poses"]})
    # `pose_only` (Roblox joint names) is the clip's contract - e.g. an upper-body
    # clip must never pose a leg or the root, or at Action priority it freezes the
    # default walk. Refuse to build a clip that breaks its own contract.
    allowed = spec.get("pose_only")
    if allowed is not None:
        bad = [j for j in posed if j not in allowed]
        if bad:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: poses {bad} outside its pose_only contract {allowed}")
    # A marker fires when playback reaches its Keyframe, so it must sit ON one.
    markers = spec.get("markers", {})
    times = [k["t"] for k in out]
    for mname, mt in markers.items():
        if not any(abs(mt - t) < 1e-6 for t in times):
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: marker {mname!r} at t={mt} is not on an authored keyframe "
                             f"({times}); author a beat at that time")
    last = max(times)
    if abs(last - spec["duration"]) > 1e-6:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: last keyframe t={last} != duration {spec['duration']}; Roblox plays "
                         f"a clip for exactly its last keyframe time")
    return {"name": name, "posed": posed, "priority": spec.get("priority", "Action"),
            "loop": bool(spec.get("loop", False)), "duration": spec["duration"], "keyframes": out,
            "markers": markers}


def _n(v):
    return ("%.4f" % v).rstrip("0").rstrip(".") or "0"


def _kfs(d):
    rows = []
    for k in d["keyframes"]:
        ps = []
        for j, v in sorted(k["poses"].items()):
            bits = []
            if "r" in v:
                bits.append("r={%s}" % ",".join(_n(x) for x in v["r"]))
            if "p" in v:
                bits.append("p={%s}" % ",".join(_n(x) for x in v["p"]))
            ps.append('["%s"]={%s}' % (j, ",".join(bits)))
        ms = [m for m, t in d["markers"].items() if abs(t - k["t"]) < 1e-6]
        mk = ",m={%s}" % ",".join('"%s"' % m for m in sorted(ms)) if ms else ""
        rows.append('{t=%s,s="%s",d="%s",poses={%s}%s}' % (_n(k["t"]), k["s"], k["d"], ",".join(ps), mk))
    return "{" + ",".join(rows) + "}"

# Roblox animation, headless

> **First time on this machine?** Read `LOCAL.md` in this folder. If it does not exist, run the
> `roblox-skills-setup` skill (or copy `LOCAL.template.md` to `LOCAL.md` and fill it in).
> `LOCAL.md` holds your paths and tool locations; it is yours and is never shared.

Author animation as **data** (a JSON spec of poses over time), bake it into a real
Blender Action, render it, and **look at the result** before believing it.

The loop is: **author → render every frame → tile into a contact sheet → look →
correct → repeat.** Everything here exists because some step of that loop caught a
failure that every other check missed.

## Read this first: the trap that wastes the most time

**Most Roblox rigs ship a Blender Action holding their rest pose.** Blender
**re-evaluates that Action during render**. So if you set pose values and then
render:

- every numeric probe reports your pose applied perfectly
- every rendered frame shows the rig's default pose
- the data and the image never reconcile, and there is no error

Clearing the Action does not help either, because **that Action IS the rest pose** —
clear it and the limbs collapse into the torso.

**The fix: insert KEYFRAMES into that same Action**, then `frame_set()` per frame
and render. The animation then *is* the Action, nothing can overwrite it, untouched
bones hold their rest values by constant extrapolation, and you end up with a real
Action — which is what a Roblox export needs anyway. `scripts/anim_render.py`
already does this.

Full list in `references/traps.md` — 28 of them. Read it before debugging anything.

## Author in FK. Not IK.

A Roblox `KeyframeSequence` is **a tree of per-joint rotations**, one per Motor6D.
That is FK. Every R15 rig ships one control bone per joint to match. Drive the
character with IK targets and you are round-tripping through a solver Roblox never
asked for, and paying for it:

- **position-only IK targets leave limb ROLL free**, so blocky Roblox parts present
  whatever face the solver picks and snap between frames. On a textured avatar that
  reads as **colours changing instantly** — the symptom that makes an animation look
  buggy
- **the solver hops between equally-good branches** frame to frame, so limbs pop
  while every frame still verifies perfectly
- it is slow

FK has no branches, no singularities, no roll ambiguity, is exactly 1:1 in degrees,
and exports straight to Roblox.

**Most rigs ship in IK mode**, which makes every `FK_*` bone read as inert. Flip the
switch — do not conclude FK is dead:

```json
"properties": {"ARM_IK_FK.L": 0.0, "ARM_IK_FK.R": 0.0,
               "LEG_IK_FK.L": 0.0, "LEG_IK_FK.R": 0.0}
```

Measured on a free community R15 rig, and pleasantly uniform: every limb rests pointing
straight **down**; on every `FK_*` bone **X negative swings forward, Z positive
swings to the character's right**, 1:1 in degrees, **identical on both sides** — no
mirror inversion. Child angles are relative to the parent.

The general lesson, whatever rig you use: **if a control bone is inert, look for a
switch that disables it before writing it off.** Rigify-style R15 rigs carry
`ARM_IK_FK` / `LEG_IK_FK` custom properties that default to `1.0` (IK). Set them to
`0.0`, key them (so `frame_set` cannot flip them back), and author in FK. The
direction conventions above were measured on one rig; `calibrate_rig.py` and
`sweep_control.py` re-measure them on yours, so run them on any rig you have not used.
Your rig's `.blend` path goes in `LOCAL.md`.

Reach for IK only when a limb must hit an exact world point. Then read traps 12–15.

## Make it look like Roblox, not like the reference

- **30 FPS**, and a combat move runs **0.3–0.7s**. The Animation Editor's default is
  30fps. Real-life timing is far too slow for a game. Take
  the **mechanics** from how the move really works; take the **timing** from Roblox.
- **Five poses**: idle, anticipation, contact, follow-through, recovery.
- **Ease per segment** — `"ease": "in"` to accelerate into the strike, `"out"` to
  settle. A fixed smoothstep decelerates into every keyframe, so the strike eases to
  a stop at its own contact frame and the whole thing reads mushy.
- **Exaggerate.** Real Roblox combat animation goes well past human range and reads
  off the silhouette.
- **Render plain grey** (`"plain": true`). A busy avatar texture turns a blocky rig
  into an unreadable jumble and you end up debugging the costume instead of the pose.
  Real Roblox animations are showcased on a plain dummy for exactly this reason.

**`references/pose-recipes.md` has the actual numbers** — measured angle tables for
guard, anticipation, chamber, contact and follow-through, the timing skeleton, and
the two rules that catch people out (shoulder + elbow must stay under ~120 total;
a high kick needs `UpperLeg X` past −120 or the leg merges with the torso). Start
from those and adjust against the preview. Do not re-derive them.

## Be fast — measured, not guessed

The whole loop is **seconds**. If a pass takes minutes, something is wrong.
Measured on a mid-range PC, one animation of 24–36 frames:

| stage | time | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Blender loads the rig | **0.7s** | startup is never the problem |
| numeric probe (whole FK control map) | **0.1s** | ask the rig questions with numbers |
| preview render (`"preview": true`) | **4–6.5s** | 1 view, 320x240, 1 sample |
| full render, 2 views @ 640x560 | **9–17s** | do this once, at the end |
| GIF encode | **0.3s** | |
| `to_roblox.py` → Luau | **0.1s** | |
| build + verify in Studio | **one `execute_luau` call** | |

**Machine time for a finished, in-Studio animation: well under a minute.** What
actually costs time is *authoring iterations*, so spend them on the preview and
never on the full render. With `references/pose-recipes.md` to start from, a
second move should land in 1–3 previews — the punch in `references/` was right on
the **first** try. The wave example was NOT: it passed every number and still read as a
hand on the head, and it took a human eye to say so (fixed 2026-10-23). Numbers prove the
pose matches the spec; only looking proves the spec is the right move.

`"report": true` prints every joint's position at each beat: when a pose looks
wrong it names the joint in one run instead of five render passes of guessing.

**Do not render to answer a question a probe can answer.**

## Non-negotiables

Each is here because skipping it shipped something broken that looked fine:

1. **Never trust a run that exited 0.** `anim_render.py` asserts rig integrity per
   frame, asserts the frames were written, and hard-exits non-zero otherwise.
2. **Look at the frames.** Every pass.
3. **With a reference, build the side-by-side and judge on that** — never on the
   render alone.
4. **Inspect the finished GIF itself**, not the PNGs you encoded it from.
5. **Never relax a tolerance to turn a red light green.** Fix the spec.

## Workflow

### 1. Calibrate the rig (any rig you have not used)

```bash
blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python scripts/calibrate_rig.py
blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python scripts/sweep_control.py -- FK_UpperLeg.R:rot TORSO:rot
```

`calibrate_rig.py` reports the deform vs control armature, the Action trap, the
**IK/FK switch state**, and which controls actually move something.
`sweep_control.py` gives each axis's direction, sign and usable range — it measures
bone *direction* as well as position, so rotation-only controls are not missed.

If the `FK_*` bones read inert, that is the IK/FK switch, not a dead rig.

### 2. Author the spec

`fps`, `duration`, `w`, `h`, `margin`, `views`, `properties`, `plain`, `preview`,
`report`, and `keyframes[]` of `{t, ease, bones: {Bone: {rot|loc|target|aim}}}`.

`rot` is what you want almost always. `loc` for controls with no end effector
(`ROOT`). `target` / `aim` are the IK escape hatch — see traps 12–15.

Three things that go wrong every time if you forget them:

- **FK child angles compound with the parent.** Shoulder 50° + elbow 70° puts the
  forearm 120° from vertical, pointing up over the shoulder. Keep shoulder + elbow
  under ~110° for a guard.
- **Lean and twist go on `UpTorso`**, which drives only the upper body. `TORSO`
  drives the legs too, so leaning it tips the figure over and slides the planted
  foot. The rig also *amplifies*: `X = +15` swings the head 23°.
- **Counter-rotate the support ankle**, `FK_Foot.X ≈ -(FK_UpperLeg.X +
  FK_LowerLeg.X)`, or the foot tilts with the leg and the character looks like it is
  standing on a slope.

See `references/example-fk-roundhouse.json` (0.8s kick) and
`references/example-fk-punch.json` (0.5s cross), plus `references/pose-recipes.md`.

### 2a. IF A PROP IS IN THE HAND, RESEARCH HOW IT IS REALLY HELD. FIRST.

**This step happens BEFORE you author a keyframe, and it is not optional.** The
moment a clip has a weapon or a tool in it, "does the pose read" stops being a
question about the rig and becomes a question about that object, which is a fact
about the world and not something to infer from a matrix.

The failure this exists to prevent, from a real build: a glaive was authored with
its head DOWN at the wielder's hip. Every downstream stage then did its job
perfectly - the engine reproduced the authored grip, the pose strip matched the
contact sheet frame for frame, grip error 0.000, zero samples of the weapon
inside the body - and the game shipped a polearm carried upside down. **A wrong
pose authored here is invisible to every check after it, because every check
after it is measuring agreement with THIS.** When a human finally
looked, the verdict was that it was upside down. They were right, and the cost was
an entire session downstream of a decision made in ten seconds here.

Before authoring:

1. **Search for how the weapon class is carried and used.** Photographs of
   practitioners, not concept art, not other games. Ten seconds of reading beats
   four rounds of guessing at numbers.
2. **Write the answer into the spec as `_intent`,** as a sentence about the
   weapon: "head up, shaft crossing the lead shoulder", "blade angled up and
   forward from a lowered hand". That sentence is what the contact sheet gets
   judged against - see step 3.
3. **Sanity-check the obvious ones from the list below** before reaching for a
   search.

| class | at rest | in a swing |
|---|---|---|
| polearm, glaive, naginata, spear | **head UP** - shouldered, planted butt-to-ground, or at a guard with the blade at chest height or above. Never hanging at the feet | the head leads the arc; the shaft crosses in front of the body, never in the same vertical plane as the arm |
| sword | angled up and forward from a **lowered** hand, around +35 degrees. Straight down reads as dropped | edge leads; the wrist is not a hinge, the whole arm carries the arc |
| axe, hammer | head up or shouldered, the weight carried high | the head is the mass - it arrives last and it arrives hardest |
| fist weapon, gauntlet | worn, not gripped; a brawler's guard, both fists up | the hips drive it, not the shoulder |

**Hold the prop in a pose the wearer's own body could get into.** A one-handed
carry of anything longer than the character is tall does not sit in the same
plane as the arm, or it clips.

### 3. Render and verify

```bash
blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python scripts/anim_render.py -- spec.json out/
ffmpeg -start_number 0 -i "out/side_%03d.png" -vf "scale=240:-1,tile=6x6" sheet.png
```

The camera frames itself on the **whole animation's** bounds and solves its distance
from the field of view, so nothing leaves frame; `margin` (default 1.10) is the only
knob. Render **at least two angles** — a right-leg kick is invisible from the left.

**Then judge the sheet against the REFERENCE, not against itself.** Open the
`_intent` sentence from step 2a and check the sheet frame by frame against it:
is the head up, is the blade leading, does the shaft cross in front of the body.
A contact sheet only ever proves that the render matches the spec. It cannot tell
you the spec was right, and every stage downstream will treat it as ground truth
- so this is the last point in the pipeline where a wrong pose is cheap to fix.
If the sheet and the reference disagree, the reference wins and the spec changes.

### 4. Deliver a GIF, then check the GIF

```bash
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -start_number 0 -i "out/side_%03d.png" -framerate 30 -start_number 0 -i "out/tq_%03d.png" -filter_complex "[0]scale=420:-1[a];[1]scale=420:-1[b];[a][b]hstack=2,split[s0][s1];[s0]palettegen=stats_mode=diff[p];[s1][p]paletteuse=dither=bayer:bayer_scale=3" -loop 0 anim.gif
```

**Read the sheet ONCE, at the size you need and no larger.** A contact sheet is
the most expensive object in this pipeline: an image is re-sent on every later
tool call in the same context, so a full-resolution sheet read early costs
hundreds of thousands of tokens by the end of a run. Tile it down, crop to the
limb in question when that is the question, and do not re-open it to re-check
something you could have measured. Where a check can be a NUMBER - does the
weapon leave the hand, does it pass through a limb, what angle does it sit at -
make it a number and read one line of text instead.

Then pull frames back out of the finished GIF and look at them — motion reads
differently from stills, and encode settings fail silently:

```bash
ffmpeg -i anim.gif -vf "select='not(mod(n,2))',tile=4x3" -vsync 0 verify.png
```

## An authored clip breaks the ones you did not author

Roblox's default `Animate` script plays idle, walk, run, jump, fall and climb at
**Core** priority. Anything you author and play at `Idle` or above **masks them
on every joint it poses**, for as long as it is playing.

So a full-body idle loop - the correct fix for a character standing there with a
weapon - stops the legs from moving when the player walks, because your clip is
posing the legs at a higher priority than the walk cycle. It looks exactly like
"the walk animation is missing", and it appears only on the character you
authored the idle for, which makes it read as a problem with that character's
weapon.

**Pick one and say which:**

- author the idle at **`Core`** priority, so the default walk still wins; or
- **do not pose the legs** in it - author only the arms and torso and let the
  default locomotion drive everything below the hips; or
- **author the locomotion set too** (walk and run at `Movement`), which is the
  only option if the carry pose has to change how the character walks.

**And check it, per character, in a playtest:** stand still, walk, run, jump,
land. Watch the LEGS. This costs about fifteen seconds per fighter and there is
no static check that can see it - the clip is correct, the rig is correct, and
the defect only exists while two clips are playing at once.

## R15 vs R6

**Prefer R15.** R15 has elbows and knees, so it has a joint for every angle a
reference shows, and FK maps one control bone to each.

**A custom-mesh R6 rig with no .blend** (rigid GLB parts + probed Motor6D C0/C1): author in
joint space with `scripts/r6_clip.py` (renders the real parts through the exact Motor6D chain,
grounds the root per key, reports foot y / stance slip / limb overlaps) and emit Luau with
`scripts/r6_luau.py` (verbatim Pose CFrames, R15 specs too, one replaced-wholesale folder).
Conversion lives in `scripts/r6_joint.py`. See traps 39-40.
A **standard R6 avatar** works the same way (proven 2026-10-22): probe the six Motor6Ds of a
`CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription(desc, Enum.HumanoidRigType.R6)` dummy (they exist in edit
mode), build box GLBs at the real part sizes at the chain's rest centres, and write rig.json;
the clip played in Studio matched the render at the contact key to 0.00002 studs.

R6 limbs are **rigid single blocks with no elbow**. A folded boxing guard is not a
pose R6 can hold at all; asking for it raises the whole arm. Use R6 only when the
game requires it, and expect stiff pose-to-pose motion — which is R6's native look,
not a defect.

## Getting it into Roblox — the full pipeline

Verified end to end, and it needs **no upload**.

```bash
# 1. author + preview until it reads right   ("preview": true)
blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python scripts/anim_render.py -- spec.json out/

# 2. generate the Studio builder for one or many specs
python scripts/to_roblox.py kick.json punch.json wave.json > build.lua
```

2b. **Prove the export before Studio:** `blender --background <rig>.blend --enable-autoexec --python scripts/rbx_axis_check.py -- spec.json --mid`.
   It compares every keyed part's full rotation between the render and the Roblox CFrame chain (traps 35-37).
   `to_roblox.py --folder ReplicatedStorage.X.Y --no-verify` emits a yield-free builder that returns a summary; spec `markers` become KeyframeMarkers.

3. Paste `build.lua` into `execute_luau`. It creates
   `ReplicatedStorage.CustomAnims` with one `KeyframeSequence` per spec, replacing
   any of the same name, then **verifies each one loads at its authored duration**
   and prints a report. Anything other than the durations you authored is a
   failure — do not move on.

4. Copy `references/studio-binder.lua` into a LocalScript under
   `StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts`, edit its `BINDS` table, and you have
   key-triggered animations on the player's character (with respawn handling) and
   optionally mirrored onto a dummy.

Spec fields the exporter reads: `rbx_name` (Studio name), `priority` (default
`Action`, which overrides the stock walk/idle), `loop`.

**No upload:** `KeyframeSequenceProvider:RegisterKeyframeSequence(seq)` returns a
ContentId you assign straight to `Animation.AnimationId`. It needs only the
Animation capability, so a LocalScript can call it at runtime — no asset upload,
no moderation, no account. Only the **bare** string works (`hash://` and
`rbxasset://` both fail). Those ids are **session-local**: fine for testing, but
publishing needs real uploaded asset IDs. **`scripts/upload_animation.py` does that
headless** (2026-10-08): dump the KeyframeSequences from Studio, rebuild each as a
real .rbxm with Rojo, upload as Open Cloud assetType `Animation`, poll, and emit
`apply_ids.luau`, which sets an `AnimationId` attribute on each sequence. Verified
lossless (80/80 poses + markers) and playable on a character, with no
right-click "Save to Roblox" by hand.

Things that will catch you (details in traps 29–34):

- Modern rigs may carry **`AnimationConstraint`**, not `Motor6D` — 15 of them and
  zero Motor6D. Animations still bind by part name and play unchanged.
- `Enum.PoseEasingStyle` has **no `Quad`** — Linear/Constant/Cubic/Elastic/Bounce.
- You **cannot** preview a pose by writing `.Transform` in edit mode; that is the
  animation channel and only the Animator applies it. Verify the axis map by
  forward kinematics through the attachments instead.
- Studio tooling has blind spots: `capture_screenshot` fails while a script tab is
  showing rather than the 3D viewport, and play-mode output may be unreachable —
  so make the runtime script **diagnose itself on screen**, as the binder does.

Coordinate systems differ: **Roblox is +Y up / −Z forward, Blender is +Z up / −Y
forward.**
